{"content": {"body": "
General Shipping Policy
Availability: Shipping is available for most non-furniture items at the buyer’s expense.
Fragile & Complex Items: Fragile, large, or highly complex lots may be outsourced to a local UPS Store for packing and shipping, which typically incurs a higher cost.
Exclusions: Items explicitly marked Not Shippable cannot be shipped through standard methods
Post-Auction Process (Shipping Saint)
Once the auction closes and your initial payment clears, you will receive an email and text message from ShippingSaint to select either local pickup or shipping.
Invoicing: If you select shipping, your items will be moved to our fulfillment area. You will receive a separate, secondary invoice for shipping, handling, and materials once your package is packed and weighed. A $15.00 handling fee is charged per invoice.
Costs, Handling, & Insurance
Handling Fee: A $15.00 handling fee is charged per invoice. This fee covers the labor required to safely transport and store your winning items from the estate sale location to our fulfillment area.
Packaging & Materials: The buyer is responsible for the direct cost of all packing materials used to secure the items (including boxes, bubble wrap, paper, etc.).
Shipping Labels: The buyer is responsible for the final carrier shipping label cost, which is calculated based on the total box size and weight. We automatically opt for the most economical carrier unless otherwise requested.
Insurance: Every shipment includes coverage insured for $100 or the final lot value (whichever is higher).
CRITICAL DEADLINES & FORFEITURE
Invoice Timeline: Shipping invoices are generally issued 3–7 days after the local pickup event concludes (large sales may take slightly longer).
Payment Window: Shipping invoices must be paid within 14 days of issuance.
Non Payment Policy: On day 15, unpaid shipping invoices will result in the forfeiture of your items without a refund, and your CTBIDS bidding privileges may be suspended. Forfeited items will be disposed of at our discretion
Special Requests & Alternative Delivery
Non-Shippable Items: If you want to request shipping for a lot marked Not Shippable, you must text (813) 734-7297 before bidding to discuss potential options.
White-Glove Delivery (Large/Heavy Items): * Often more cost-effective than freight; requires no boxing or palletizing.
Includes vetted drivers, blanket-wrapped transport, and inside delivery.
Timeline: Requires a 24–48 hour notice. Expect roughly 2–3 weeks for pickup and an additional 2–3 weeks for delivery depending on the route. Providing photos of your space helps us book this faster.
Freight Shipping: Available for oversized items. Rates are determined by size, destination, urgency, and the greater of actual vs. dimensional weight.
Purchase Protection (via Seel)
Coverage Options: \"Make It Returnable\" (eligible for returns within 7 days of delivery/pickup) and \"Delivery Guarantee\" protection are available for purchase during checkout or automatically included with a Premier Membership.
Claims & Support: * File or track a claim directly at
resolve.seel.com
.
For questions regarding protection, email
Returns@Seel.com
.
Note: The original buyer’s premium and shipping fees are strictly non-refundable.

description:
Add a touch of classic elegance to your wrist with this beautiful vintage sterling silver bracelet featuring an intricate woven design.
Specifications:
Design: Intricate woven/mesh style with a beautiful textured finish.
Metal Purity: Sterling Silver (.925)
Size: 7" long—perfect for a classic, comfortable fit.
Total Weight: 11 grams
A highly versatile, timeless piece that layers beautifully with other bracelets or stands out beautifully on its own. Please refer to the high-resolution photos to view the clasp mechanism, hallmark stamps, and overall pre-owned estate condition.

description:
Artist Unknown
Profile of Man Smoking Pipe
Hand-Carved Wood Relief Plaque
13" x 9" x 1.5"
Unsigned
This expressive hand-carved wooden relief plaque depicts a man in profile smoking a long-stemmed pipe. Executed in a traditional folk art style, the piece features intricate textural details in the hair and a stylized geometric pattern along the lower shoulder edge. The warm, rich brown tones and lustrous finish enhance the sculptural depth, showcasing skilled craftsmanship and mid-century ethnographic influence.
Deep relief carving creates a significant dimensional presence for wall display
Features an integrated metal hanging loop on the reverse side
Hand-finished surface highlights the natural grain and character of the wood
Condition:
Good vintage condition with minor surface wear consistent with age. A small, stable separation is present where the pipe stem meets the base, and there are minor inventory markings in white ink on the reverse. The wood remains structurally sound with a vibrant finish.

Natural Amethyst Geode Cluster Deep Purple Crystals Medium 10-15 cm
This natural amethyst geode cluster features deep purple crystals on one side and a rough, unpolished rock matrix on the other. The crystals show good clarity with a rich violet color and vary in size, displaying a layered structure transitioning from purple to clear and white at the edges. The specimen measures approximately 10-15 cm in length. It is in used but well-preserved condition with no visible damage or repairs. There are no manufacturer marks or branding, as this is a naturally occurring mineral specimen suitable for collectors, crystal enthusiasts, or as a decorative piece.
4 x 4 x 3 in

description:
Pressed Glass Insulator Lot - 12 Pieces
Whitall Tatum, Armstrong, and Pyrex
Aqua, Clear, and Smoky, Vintage 1920s-1950s
This collection features twelve vintage glass telephone and telegraph insulators from prominent American manufacturers. These pieces represent a significant era in telecommunications history, showcasing various industrial glass formulas including standard aqua, clear, and heat-resistant Pyrex borosilicate glass. Matching sets and mixed lots from these manufacturers are highly collectible for their industrial aesthetic and historical utility.
Pieces Included:
Whitall Tatum Co. No. 1, Aqua Glass - characteristic greenish-blue tint, molded manufacturer marks on base
Pyrex Clear Glass Insulator - high-clarity borosilicate glass, marked "Pyrex Reg. U.S. Pat. Off."
Armstrong "W" in Triangle Mark, Aqua Glass - produced after Armstrong's 1938 acquisition of Whitall Tatum
Armstrong T.W. Smoky/Clear Glass - industrial clear glass with age-appropriate tinting and molded date codes
Additional assorted aqua and clear pressed glass insulators to complete the 12-piece set
Condition:
The lot is in good vintage condition consistent with outdoor industrial use. Several pieces show characteristic rust staining near the thread interior and top grooves from contact with metal mounting brackets. No significant structural cracks observed. Minor fleabites and surface scratches may be present on rims or skirts. All molded lettering remains legible.

description:
Waterman Paris
Striped Lacquer Fountain Pen - Gold Trim
Late 20th Century, France
This Waterman Paris fountain pen exemplifies the elegant French design and reliable engineering that defined the brand's production after moving operations to France in the mid-20th century. Featuring a slim, sophisticated profile, the barrel and cap are finished in a dark lacquer with subtle vertical burgundy stripes, complemented by gold-tone accents and rings. The Waterman brand, established in 1884, is renowned for inventing the first functional fountain pen feed, a legacy of quality visible in this late vintage example.

Includes original blue Waterman Paris presentation box with white satin lining
Original user manual booklet and one blue ink cartridge included
Condition:

The gold trim is bright and free of pitting or significant tarnish. The nib appears clean and well-maintained. The presentation box and paperwork are in very good condition with minor shelf wear to the outer casing.

Sheaffer
Lady Sheaffer Fountain Pen - Gold-Tone Brushed Finish
Vintage (Circa 1958-1960s), 1 Pen with Case
This Lady Sheaffer fountain pen represents the intersection of mid-century fashion and high-quality craftsmanship from one of America's most prestigious pen manufacturers. Part of the "Skripsert" line launched in the late 1950s, these pens were designed specifically as stylish accessories for women, often featuring clip-less designs or refined jewelry-like finishes. This specific example features a sophisticated brushed gold-tone finish complemented by an intricate, ornate engraved band on the cap, showcasing the brand's commitment to both utility and style during the peak of fountain pen production.

Distinctive brushed metal body with an ornate floral scroll engraved band on the cap
Includes original blue textured hard shell case with satin-lined interior
Accompanied by the internal metal cartridge sleeve/converter housing

description:
Natural Specimen
Quartz Geode Crystal Cluster
Mineral on Green Host Rock Matrix
Approximately 3.5" x 2.5" x 2"
Unsigned
This striking natural geode specimen features a cavity of sparkling clear quartz crystals nestled within a vibrant, teal-green host rock matrix. The exterior coloration suggests the presence of copper-bearing minerals such as chrysocolla or malachite, providing a dramatic visual contrast to the prismatic crystalline interior. This piece serves as a sophisticated organic accent, showcasing the raw geological beauty and complex textures found in natural mineral formations.
Features a well-defined interior cavity lined with translucent quartz crystal clusters
Natural green and turquoise-toned host rock with earthy iron-oxide inclusions on the reverse
Unique asymmetrical form suitable for shelf, desk, or cabinet display
Condition:
Excellent natural condition. As a raw geological specimen, it retains its original jagged edges and characteristic surface variations. The crystal points appear well-preserved within the cavity, and the surrounding matrix is stable with minor natural surface wear typical of extracted mineral specimens.

Multi-Specimen Crystal and Geode Lot
Natural Stone, Quartz, Amethyst, and Pyrite
Unsigned
This mineral and crystal collection features a diverse array of geological specimens, totaling approximately 7 pounds. The lot includes unique pyrite clusters accented with decorative pewter miniatures-a prospector and a forest scene-typical of late 20th-century gift specimens. A variety of open quartz geodes, a large polished heart, and various raw specimens provide a wide range of textures and colors for the collector.

description:
Natural Mineral Specimen
Amethyst and Rose Quartz Crystal Collection
Natural Stone Clusters and Points
Largest piece approx. 3.5" x 3"; Total weight 1.5 lbs
Unsigned
This diverse collection features a variety of natural mineral specimens, highlighted by a substantial amethyst druzy cluster with a characteristic dark, possibly copper or silicate-rich matrix. The lot includes six individual pieces showcasing different geological formations, including deep violet amethyst clusters, translucent rose quartz, and raw crystal points. The pieces demonstrate a beautiful range of color saturation and crystalline structures, making them excellent examples for geological study or natural home decor.
Features one large amethyst druzy specimen with a distinct teal-colored matrix back
Includes 6 individual pieces consisting of amethyst clusters, points, and rose quartz
Total combined weight of the specimens is 1.495 lbs (measured on scale)
Largest cluster measures approximately 3.5 inches in width according to Westcott ruler
Condition:
Very good natural condition. These are raw mineral specimens and feature natural inclusions, terminations, and matrix variations inherent to their formation. The crystal points are largely intact with expected minor abrasions consistent with raw extraction. No evidence of artificial dyes or repairs.
This is a pre-owned item donated to Goodwill of Northern Michigan.
